approval.rationale: Bootstrap registration of the independently reviewed Safe Purge v0.1 behavior already present before this governance gate.

identity.name: Safe Purge v0.1
identity.purpose: Move exact, sealed market-bar Raw and Curated physical snapshot pairs out of active archive globs into same-volume quarantine without permanent deletion.

implementation_bindings.rationale: The purge module owns sealed planning, execution, no-replace evidence publication, quarantine movement, rollback, and idempotent recovery.
The public Python API delegates purge requests to the service-owned Safe Purge boundary.
The Console backend exposes only reviewed preview, exact-confirmation execution, and stale-preview invalidation.
The Console UI is a non-authoritative adapter that invalidates reviewed plans whenever scope changes and never performs storage mutation directly.
The Catalog stores the purge lifecycle index and owns the atomic durable SUCCESS transition, while immutable JSON remains detailed evidence.

initiators: market-vault purge-plan and purge-execute CLI callers
Console preview and exact-confirmation execute actions
forbidden_bypass_layers: Console widgets must not mutate Parquet, quarantine, or DuckDB directly
API adapters must not move files outside purge_execute
storage helpers must not authorize an unsealed or stale plan

mutated_assets: Complete Raw and Curated market_bars Parquet pairs sealed by ingestion run
Same-volume quarantine paths preserving original data-root-relative paths
Immutable purge plan, precommit, and result JSON evidence
DuckDB market-bar views refreshed after movement or rollback
excluded_assets: Ingestion runs, collection manifests, and quality reports
Arbitrary external user paths and consumers

allowed_transitions.rationale: Planning may seal a non-executable refusal when physical scope or evidence is unsafe.
An exact confirmed executable plan may begin under the lifecycle lock.
A non-committed failed attempt may retry after all sealed identities are revalidated.
A pre-commit failure records non-success evidence after rollback is attempted.
Only the atomic Catalog commit with precommit and result hashes makes success authoritative.

forbidden_transitions.rationale: A completed exact plan is handled as an idempotent read and publication recovery, not restarted mutation.
Post-commit publication failure cannot roll back or demote the authoritative Catalog commit.
A refused sealed plan is never executable.
SUCCESS cannot be assigned without a new EXECUTING attempt and atomic commit.

commit_point.durable_authority: Catalog.commit_purge_operation atomically changes the exact EXECUTING row to SUCCESS and binds plan hash, immutable precommit path, terminal result path, result hash, and completion time.
commit_point.success_authoritative_when: The Catalog SUCCESS transaction commits only after all planned files are in verified quarantine and immutable precommit evidence seals the complete canonical terminal result.

pre_commit: A crash may leave some sealed files in quarantine and a Catalog state other than SUCCESS.
A pre-commit failure attempts reverse-order rollback and refreshes active market-bar views.
Immutable precommit evidence is non-terminal and must never by itself prove SUCCESS.
post_commit: Rollback is no longer legal after Catalog SUCCESS commits.
A crash may leave only non-terminal staging residue while the final result path remains absent.
An exact retry reconstructs and atomically publishes the precommitted terminal bytes after revalidation.

restorable: Before commit, files moved by the current attempt are moved back to their sealed active paths in reverse order.
A duplicated POSIX link created before unlink failure is removed only after both names and hashes verify.
non_restorable: After Catalog SUCCESS, automatic rollback is prohibited because quarantine is authoritative.
Safe Purge v0.1 provides no restore operation and no permanent deletion operation.
interruption_detection: Catalog EXECUTING or FAILED state cannot be interpreted as SUCCESS.
Catalog SUCCESS with absent terminal result triggers exact precommit-based publication recovery.
Any quarantine, Catalog, plan, precommit, or result identity conflict fails closed.

same_request_retry: The same sealed plan ID is reloaded and content-hash verified.
A failed non-committed attempt may retry only after exact active or quarantine identities and Catalog run bindings verify.
completed_retry: A Catalog SUCCESS retry performs no market-data movement.
A byte-identical existing final result is accepted; an absent final is republished from the immutable precommit.
conflicting_retry: A different plan hash, scope, run binding, quarantine identity, precommit, Catalog result hash, or final result is refused without overwrite.

lock_authority: MarketBarLifecycleLock uses exclusive atomic directory creation under the configured data root and never auto-reclaims stale locks.
lock_scope: purge_execute holds the market-bar lifecycle lock across revalidation, movement, Catalog commit, publication attempt, rollback, and view refresh.
collect_history and operation-wide collect_history_backfill use the same lifecycle boundary.
under_lock_revalidation: Every planned ingestion run and Raw/Curated identity is re-resolved before mutation.
Matching RUNNING runs and unplanned matching active snapshots are refused.
concurrent_behavior: A concurrent supported market-bar writer or purge cannot acquire the lock and must fail closed.
Read-only queries may fail or retry during transition but must not infer missing active data as successful purge evidence.

identities: Exact plan ID, canonical plan content hash, scope, target list, and plan-file location
Exact ingestion run ID, status, Raw path, Curated path, symbols, date, interval, requested session, adjustment, source, and schema version
Every target relative path, byte size, SHA-256, row count, symbols, dates, and request-key facts
Active and quarantine file identity, same-filesystem destination, and absence of unplanned matching snapshots
drift_behavior: Any missing, changed, one-sided, co-located, unsafe, newly matching, or otherwise unprovable identity refuses before additional mutation.
Execution never rewrites or splits immutable Parquet to satisfy narrower logical scope.

authoritative_evidence: Catalog purge_operations state SUCCESS with exact plan hash, precommit path, final result path, result hash, and completion timestamp
Immutable precommit containing the complete canonical proposed terminal result and matching result hash
Complete canonical final result atomically published without replacement, or recoverably absent immediately after commit
non_success_evidence: PLANNED, REFUSED, EXECUTING, or FAILED Catalog state
Plan JSON, failure result JSON, precommit JSON, staging residue, or quarantined files without Catalog SUCCESS
A partial, malformed, hash-conflicting, or unflushed terminal result
integrity_binding: Canonical JSON bytes bind every terminal result field including message and timestamps to SHA-256.
Catalog result_hash and immutable precommit terminal_result_hash must equal the canonical final bytes.
Atomic no-replace publication never overwrites a conflicting final result.

invalidation_triggers: Any Console Purge scope field modification after Preview invalidates the reviewed plan.
confirmation_invalidation: Scope modification clears exact confirmation and disables Execute until a new Preview succeeds.
execution_policy: Execution requires the exact text PURGE followed by one space and the sealed plan ID.
The backend reloads the plan rather than trusting mutable widget state.

lifecycle_unit: One ingestion run's complete Raw plus Curated immutable Parquet pair is the minimum physical lifecycle unit.
partial_mutation: A one-sided pair or partial symbol/date/request-key selection within a co-located file refuses the entire plan.
An interrupted multi-file move remains non-success until rollback or committed recovery completes.
rollback_expectation: Before commit, every file moved by the attempt is rolled back when safely provable.
Rollback uncertainty is reported and never converted into terminal SUCCESS.

retained_dependents: Committed Verified Canonical builds with embedded source hashes and provenance
Committed Dataset artifacts that verify without reloading Canonical
Committed Dataset Catalog snapshots that verify without reloading recorded Dataset paths
Ingestion runs, collection manifests, and quality reports
refused_cases: Co-located symbols, dates, or request-key facts outside the exact requested scope
Wildcard scope, arbitrary paths, path drift, Catalog drift, or unverified reparse points
unsupported_cases: Cascade mutation of Canonical, Dataset, or Dataset Catalog artifacts
Discovery or lifecycle guarantees for arbitrary external user code and paths
Restore, garbage collection, quarantine expiry, and permanent deletion

permanent_deletion.rationale: Safe Purge v0.1 only moves exact immutable snapshot pairs into retained same-volume quarantine and exposes no permanent-delete command or API.

implementation_tests: Exact whole-physical-batch and complete co-located multi-symbol purge succeeds
Partial co-located scope, one-sided pairs, drift, bad confirmation, tampering, reparse paths, and lock conflicts refuse
Pre-commit failures roll back without terminal SUCCESS evidence
Post-commit terminal publication interruption recovers exact canonical bytes idempotently
Existing committed Canonical, Dataset, and Dataset Catalog artifacts remain independently verifiable after source quarantine
Console scope changes invalidate Preview and confirmation
